traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for Story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION are satisfied based on concrete implementation and tests:
1) Core Functionality - Implemented by the valid-req-reference rule and its helpers. The rule parses annotations, resolves story paths, reads story files, extracts requirement IDs, and reports reqMissing when referenced IDs do not exist. Tests explicitly verify both successful matches and missing-requirement scenarios.
2) Quality Standards (various formats and structures) - Requirement IDs are extracted using a generic /REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g regex over full markdown files, so requirements embedded as headings, inline text, bullet items, or numbered items are all supported. - Tests exercise different structures: core story files, a bullet-list fixture, and multi-story fixtures with reused IDs. - This demonstrates the validator works across varied story formats and structures, not tied to a single rigid pattern.
3) Integration - The rule is exported from src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts, registered dynamically in src/index.ts, and enabled in both recommended and strict flat-config presets with severity "error". - Plugin config tests confirm valid-req-reference is part of the plugin rules and configs alongside other validation rules, showing it integrates into the existing annotation and file-validation workflow.
4) User Experience - Error messages are concise and specific: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'" and "Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'". - Tests assert messageId and data for both missing requirements and invalid paths, ensuring developers see clear, parameterized diagnostics referencing both the requirement ID and the story path.
5) Error Handling - File reading and parsing are wrapped in try/catch; on any I/O or parsing error, the cache is populated with an empty Set instead of throwing, so linting remains robust even with malformed or unreadable story files. - Path-validation logic rejects traversal and absolute paths with a dedicated invalidPath diagnostic instead of failing unexpectedly. - Together, this fulfills the requirement to handle malformed files, missing sections, and parsing errors gracefully.
6) Documentation - docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md documents the purpose and behavior of requirement content validation, ties it back to this story, and includes multiple concrete examples of correct and incorrect usage, covering both @req and @supports.
While some advanced ideas in the story’s implementation notes (like timestamp-based cache invalidation or configurable regex patterns for story-internal requirement IDs) are not implemented, they are not part of the explicit acceptance criteria or requirement list. The implemented functionality fully covers all stated requirements (REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-FORMAT via generic matching, REQ-DEEP-SECTION via whole-file scanning, REQ-DEEP-CACHE via a shared Map, and REQ-DEEP-ERROR via explicit diagnostics), and all associated tests are passing. Therefore, this story is considered fully implemented and passes.
